nv_swamp_cave.blurb: Swamp Cave is a shaded cave at the back of the narrow Arrow Canyon, northeast of Las Vegas in southern Nevada. It holds 17 sport routes and nothing else, so bring only quickdraws and a rope. The grades start around 5.10 and are concentrated between 5.11 and 5.13, with a single route at the very top of the range, which makes it a place for strong climbers rather than beginners. The walk in follows the canyon floor until the cave opens on the left. Because it sits so deep in the canyon, it is rarely crowded, and you will often have the cave to yourself.

nv_cloud_tower.blurb: Cloud Tower is a freestanding sandstone pillar on the northeast flank of Rainbow Mountain's east peak, in Juniper Canyon at Red Rock, west of Las Vegas. It is a purely traditional objective with 16 routes, most of them multi-pitch, running from moderate 5.8 and 5.9 climbs through a solid group of 5.10s to a few at 5.12. The approach is a long uphill slog from the Pine Creek side, so plan a big day with a heavy pack and an early start. The hard work pays off in quiet, sustained crack climbing well away from the roadside crowds.

nv_observatory_the.blurb: The Observatory is a sandstone wall just south of The Gallery in the Second Pullout area of the Calico Hills, and it can be spotted from the parking lot. Of its 16 routes, 14 are bolted sport and two are trad, with a steep, vertical upper face, a fourth-class scramble in the middle and a corridor at the base. Grades run from easy 5.5 to 5.11, and the single biggest cluster sits at 5.9, so it suits climbers stepping up to multi-pitch sport. The upper face gets exposed to wind, and the sun reaches it from late morning onward.

nv_ultraman_wall.blurb: Ultraman Wall is a sunny sandstone slab in the First Pullout area of the Calico Hills at Red Rock, west of Panty Wall. It has 16 routes, a mix of sport and trad, mostly between 5.6 and 5.9 with a single 5.10. The slab climbing here is sparsely protected, so it rewards solid footwork and a calm head, and it is better suited to experienced leaders than to someone on a first 5.8. Many lines carry the names of Japanese movie monsters. Bring a light trad rack alongside quickdraws, and consider a second rope.

nv_friar_and_byrd_pinnacle_the.blurb: The Friar and Byrd Pinnacle is a tall column of sandstone in Oak Creek Canyon at Red Rock, west of Las Vegas, topped by a huge balanced boulder that makes it an easy landmark to spot from the trail. Of its 16 routes, 15 are traditional and one is bolted. They climb from 5.8 up to a single 5.13, with most between 5.9 and 5.10, including both single-pitch cracks and two-pitch lines. You reach the base by walking the Oak Creek trail toward Solar Slab, then branching off beneath the column. A full trad rack is the right tool here.
